title: Fewest Two-Seat Rafts
statement:
A group has to cross a river. weights[i] is the weight of person i. Every raft can carry at most two people, and their total weight must not exceed limit. Nobody weighs more than limit, so everyone fits alone.

Return the fewest rafts needed to carry everyone. Each raft makes one trip.

examples.why: The weight limit is generous, but a raft still has only two seats.
Pairing the two lightest (1 + 2) leaves 4 and 5 to go alone: 3 rafts. Pairing 1 + 5 and 2 + 4 needs only 2.

hints: The heaviest person needs a raft no matter what. Who, if anyone, should share it?
If the lightest person cannot ride with the heaviest, nobody can. So the heaviest goes alone. If the lightest can, pairing them never hurts.
Sort, then use one pointer at the light end and one at the heavy end. Each raft takes the heavy person, plus the light one when they fit together.

explain.intuition:
Look at the heaviest person. They take a raft whatever happens. The best companion is the lightest person: if even the lightest does not fit, the heaviest rides alone. If the lightest does fit, pairing them is safe. Any other plan can swap the lightest into that seat without breaking a raft, since the person swapped out is at least as heavy.

After sorting, two pointers make this cheap: hi walks down from the heaviest, lo walks up from the lightest, and every step fills one raft. Pairing the two lightest first, which feels natural, wastes the seat a heavy person needed.
steps: While lo ≤ hi: if weights[lo] + weights[hi] ≤ limit, move lo right. Always move hi left and add a raft.
pitfalls: Pairing the two lightest people first, which fails on the third example.
Forgetting the two-seat rule and packing as many people as the weight allows.
Using lo < hi as the loop condition and forgetting the last single person when the count is odd.

solutions.title: Sort and pair the ends
solutions.idea: The heaviest left takes a raft, with the lightest left if they fit.

solutions.title: Count weights instead of sorting
solutions.idea: Weights are bounded by limit, so count how many people have each weight and run the same two-pointer greedy over the counts.

followups: Rafts can carry up to three people. Does the greedy still work?
Each raft can make several trips and you have only m rafts. How many trips are needed?
